MICROECONOMICS
MICRO-33
Time: 5 minutes
Outcome: Trace entry, exit, zero economic profit, normal profit, and long-run competitive adjustment.
Difficulty: Intermediate
THE CORE IDEA

Entry and exit move a competitive industry toward long-run equilibrium with zero economic profit. More firms supply more total output at each price. At long-run equilibrium the firm maximizes profit and entry/exit has eliminated economic profit. Entry and exit remove persistent economic profit or loss in the benchmark model.
HOW TO RECOGNIZE IT
At long-run equilibrium the firm maximizes profit and entry/exit has eliminated economic profit.
Entry and exit remove persistent economic profit or loss in the benchmark model.
Long-run industry assessment 10: Demand falls in a constant-cost industry and some firms leave.
Long-run industry assessment 11: Demand rises in a constant-cost industry and entry is unrestricted.
WATCH OUT

Do not miss long run equilibrium conditions. At long-run equilibrium the firm maximizes profit and entry/exit has eliminated economic profit. Entry and exit remove persistent economic profit or loss in the benchmark model.
WORKED EXAMPLE: ENTRY AND ZERO ECONOMIC PROFIT

The market equilibrium price is $25. At that price, the representative firm produces 50 units where P = MC, and $25 is also the minimum ATC. Revenue covers all explicit and implicit costs, so economic profit is zero and no entry or exit pressure remains.
